confirmed.title: README labels the Antigravity plugin target 'Gemini IDE'; Gemini CLI users aren't pointed to ~/.agents/skills

Add a smoke test that installs to each advertised host and confirms the host finds the skills.

confirmed.title: Architect decision trees conflict; 'high scalability → microservices' contradicts the monolith-first guidance

confirmed.title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY: transaction-wrapping ignored and failure guidance wrong
confirmed.evidence: The skill recommends CIC with no warning that it can't run in a transaction block, and most runners wrap migrations in one. :127 'may fail silently ... re-run if needed'. A failure actually errors and leaves an INVALID index, and the :233 query returns OIDs, not names.
confirmed.impact: Migrations fail at deploy time, the agent may drop CONCURRENTLY, and an invalid index lingers.
confirmed.recommendation: Give per-tool non-transactional opt-outs, one CIC per migration, and recovery via DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS / REINDEX CONCURRENTLY with a named query.
confirmed.verifierCorrection: The defect is real but medium, not high. Both failures are loud, recoverable deploy errors with no data loss, and the skill's own staging check (:215-225) and the pg_index check at :233, which works apart from returning OIDs, would surface them.

confirmed.title: backend-migrate has no confirmation gate or execution boundary for DDL, backfills, drops or restores on real DBs
confirmed.evidence: The workflow ends 'Test on staging ... Deploy' without saying who runs it or against which DB. Grep confirm|mode=auto: 0. There is no reference check or backup check before contract.
confirmed.impact: In default auto mode the agent may run DDL or mass UPDATEs against a prod or staging DATABASE_URL.
confirmed.recommendation: The skill writes files plus a runbook and applies them only to a verified local DB. It always pauses on DROP, type change, backfill, restore or down migrations, and checks references and backups before contract.
confirmed.verifierCorrection: The shared mode=auto contract (tool-rules.md:36-38) already pauses on schema drops, data deletion and production deploys. What is actually missing: backend-migrate does not reference that contract, gives no rule for verifying the target database (local only versus a remote DATABASE_URL), and has no explicit pause for mass backfill UPDATEs, type changes, restores or down migrations, and no concrete reference or backup check step before contract. Severity is medium.

confirmed.title: Rename guidance never carries UNIQUE, NOT NULL, indexes or dependents to the new column

confirmed.verifierCorrection: The gap is real but partly mitigated by the required principles.md:9. Most dependent-object breakage (views) is a loud DROP failure, not silent. The real risk is that copying the example leaves contact_email without UNIQUE or NOT NULL. Severity is medium.

Treat the 'Email already registered' example as a minor wording inconsistency, not a contradiction. Severity is medium, not high.

confirmed.title: GraphQL and gRPC claimed but only REST/OpenAPI has working guidance

confirmed.title: CSRF and session hardening are missing for cookie-borne credentials
confirmed.evidence: :263 'CSRF protection if using cookie-based sessions' is the only mention, while :262 puts the access token in a cookie and :120 allows SameSite None. Grep fixation|regenerate|idle: 0.

confirmed.verifierCorrection: The line reference should be :261 (access token in cookie), not :262. Note that the Lax/Strict defaults at :52 and :119 partly mitigate CSRF. The remaining gaps are: no CSRF mechanism for SameSite=None or cookie-JWT setups, no session-ID regeneration, and no idle or absolute timeouts. Severity is medium.

confirmed.title: Idempotency keys are mandated but no implementation pattern is given

confirmed.impact: Retries can double-charge or double-create records.
confirmed.recommendation: Add an Idempotency-Key contract, an idempotency_keys table, fingerprint mismatch → 422, in-flight duplicate → 409, response replay, and tests.
confirmed.verifierCorrection: Severity is medium: a missing implementation pattern for a principle that is mandated, not a high-impact defect.

confirmed.title: No guidance for inbound or outbound webhooks (raw body, signature, dedup, retries, SSRF)

confirmed.verifierCorrection: Credit implement:325 and ops:179-184 (outbox) for outbound delivery and retries. The missing pieces are inbound signature verification on the raw body, dedup and replay protection, and SSRF and signing guidance for outbound targets. Also note that auth:67 combined with :70 (hash-only storage) is wrong for HMAC webhook secrets.

confirmed.title: backend-implement and backend-refactor both trigger on refactor/split, with conflicting workflows
confirmed.evidence: implement :3 'add, split, or refactor' and has its own split workflow with no baseline or characterization step. refactor :17 forbids mixing refactors with features, and grep backend-refactor in implement returns 0.

confirmed.title: Tests and the app run autonomously with no check that the DB, queues or integrations are isolated

confirmed.verifierCorrection: Drop the EXPLAIN ANALYZE claim and the 'real database' framing. Narrow the gap to this: there is no pre-run check of the target environment before auto-running the suite (test:30-33) or `npm start` in the doctor smoke test (doctor:136-142), even though test:73 asks for a separate test DB. A target that is not local or ephemeral should be a pause condition.

confirmed.title: backend-implement writes and suggests applying migrations, bypassing backend-migrate and any gate
confirmed.evidence: :235 'Add the migration that matches the database decision'. :208 'Next steps: review, migrate, run'. Grep backend-migrate: 0.

That can produce locking or breaking DDL that ships later. Severity medium.

confirmed.title: Refactor baseline hides failures (tee), writes into the repo, and its output hash can never match
confirmed.evidence: `npm test 2>&1 | tee baseline-output.txt` returns tee's exit 0. 'Record the test output hash'. 'identical output' is the exit condition. On resume a hash mismatch means re-baseline. Durations and seeds vary, and characterization tests add output.
confirmed.impact: A red baseline looks green, the exit condition is unreachable, resume re-baselines on half-refactored code, and the stray file may be committed.
confirmed.recommendation: Use pipefail/$LASTEXITCODE, compare per-test pass/fail from JUnit/JSON allowing added tests, store artifacts under .checkpoints, and verify against the original baseline on resume.

confirmed.title: Refactor size and strangler rules can't be met for atomic or large in-process changes
confirmed.evidence: :137 '>~5 files, break it down'. :266 lsp_rename touches every caller. :290 '>20 files: Use the strangler-fig pattern' (routing or flags), but :166 says 'Never ship a partially-refactored state'. A javax→jakarta bump can't be split.
confirmed.impact: The agent either loops on splitting the change, adds needless flags, or breaks the rules.
confirmed.recommendation: Exempt tool-driven mechanical changes. Use a facade for in-process splits, keep strangler fig for service replacement, and define 'partial' as 'not green'.
confirmed.verifierCorrection: Medium, not high. The contradiction is softened by the approximate threshold and by the alias approach at :196. What should change: :290 should point in-process renames and moves to the alias/facade approach rather than strangler fig, :166 should say 'partial' means 'not green', and mechanical or atomic changes (tool-driven renames, framework namespace bumps) need an exemption.

confirmed.title: Canonical implement snippets persist the raw DTO (plaintext password), race on uniqueness and leak fields
confirmed.evidence: `findByEmail` → throw → `repo.create(dto)` where the DTO has `password`. FastAPI has no response_model and returns an un-awaited sync call from async def. Gin's ShouldBindJSON has no return on error.
confirmed.impact: Plaintext passwords get stored, duplicates race, password_hash is serialized, and execution continues on bad input.
confirmed.recommendation: Hash the password, map explicit fields, rely on the unique constraint, add response_model/Annotated, and return after the 400.
confirmed.verifierCorrection: Keep the confirmed issues: missing await or blocking call and no response_model in FastAPI, no return after the 400 in Gin, a check-then-insert race with no mapping of the unique violation, and the entity returned without explicit field mapping. Downgrade 'persists plaintext password' to a risk of copying the snippet, since the DTO's fields are not shown and hashing is required elsewhere. Severity medium.

confirmed.title: OpenCode/OMO tool names and LSP-dependent gates have no CLI fallback on the advertised Cursor and Gemini hosts

The README and package.json are Opencode-centric ('Usage in Opencode'), which lowers the impact on the other hosts.

confirmed.title: 'Update invalid tests ... re-run until green' lets the agent weaken or skip failing tests
confirmed.evidence: :203-204 'Fix code bugs or update tests that are now invalid / Re-run until green', run in auto mode. No criteria are given, nothing forbids skip/xfail, and the loop has no cap.

confirmed.title: No performance investigation, profiling, load testing or before/after measurement
confirmed.evidence: Grep load test|k6|locust|profil|pprof|pg_stat_statements|bisect: 0. Doctor's perf tree jumps straight to 'Consider caching'. 'Performance | B' is graded but never measured.

confirmed.title: Health endpoint paths contradict between ops, deploy and doctor
confirmed.evidence: ops '/health, /ready, /metrics'. deploy '/health/live', '/health/ready'. doctor probes /health or /ready. The ops Go snippet uses net/http while implement uses Gin.
confirmed.impact: Production Readiness creates duplicate probe sets and doctor raises false 'missing health endpoint' findings.

confirmed.verifierCorrection: The evidence is accurate. ops:104 lists '/health, /ready, /metrics' and ops:265-267/291-295/315-320 scaffold /health. deploy:206-207/212 uses /health/live and /health/ready. doctor:141 curls /health or /ready, and doctor:282 recommends 'Add /health and /ready'. The ops audit grep at :250 matches only the quoted literal '/health', so it would not detect deploy's /health/live and could raise the High 'missing /health' finding (ops:347). ops:317 registers on net/http DefaultServeMux, while implement:159/293 standardises on Gin. Severity is overstated, though. The impact is duplicate endpoints and false-positive findings, not dangerous or materially wrong behaviour, so medium.

confirmed.title: backend-deploy templates are Node-only though it detects Python, Go and Java
confirmed.evidence: Every template uses node:20-alpine, npm ci, setup-node, a TS readiness handler and NODE_ENV. Grep python|go build|java|gradle: only the manifest glob.
confirmed.impact: Non-Node projects get a pipeline that can't build.
confirmed.recommendation: Add per-stack Dockerfile and CI references selected from the manifest, and derive build/start commands and port from the project.

confirmed.title: backend-deploy has no confirmation gates for pushes, deploys or overwriting existing pipelines
confirmed.evidence: Grep mode=|confirm|kubectl|terraform finds nothing relevant. The template has `push: true`, and there is no 'detect existing Dockerfile/CI' step.
confirmed.impact: The agent may replace a working CI pipeline or push or apply to environments without asking.
confirmed.recommendation: Generate files automatically, but confirm push, apply, IaC and secret changes. Diff and patch existing artifacts rather than overwriting them.
confirmed.verifierCorrection: The part to keep is that there is no step to detect existing artifacts. Deploy's prerequisites (:22-40) glob only source dirs and manifests, and a grep for existing, overwrite, already, .github or gitlab-ci in deploy returns nothing. So the agent may regenerate over a working Dockerfile or workflow. The push and apply claim is overstated. The skill never tells the agent to run docker push, kubectl, helm or terraform. `push: true` (:172) and `docker push` (:192) are CI steps that run in GitHub or GitLab after a merge to main, which is normal CI. _shared/tool-rules.md:38 already requires pausing for 'production deploys', 'secret rotation' and 'force-pushes', and :59 provides a git-checkout rollback for generated files. Overwrites are recoverable through git, so this is medium, not high.

confirmed.title: Templates pin EOL or deprecated versions (Node 20, docker:24, npm --only, OpenAPI 3.0, safety check)
confirmed.evidence: `node:20-alpine` (Node 20 went EOL 2026-04-30), `docker:24`, `npm ci --only=production`, `openapi: 3.0.0`. No 'as of' date anywhere.
confirmed.impact: Generated images run on an unpatched runtime and use deprecated flags.
confirmed.recommendation: Derive the version from .nvmrc/engines or current LTS, pin by digest, use --omit=dev, and date the examples.
confirmed.verifierCorrection: Keep: node:20-alpine at deploy:60/:67/:181 and node-version 20 at :152 (Node 20 reached EOL on 2026-04-30, before today's date of 2026-10-31). docker:24 and docker:24-dind at :188-189 are several majors behind and out of support. `npm ci --only=production` at :65 is deprecated, still works with a warning, and should be --omit=dev. There is no 'as of' date anywhere. Drop: `openapi: 3.0.0` (api-design:178/181) is neither EOL nor deprecated. OAS 3.0.x is still a valid, widely supported spec and 3.1/3.2 are merely newer, so this is an enhancement, not a defect. The 'safety check' item is not in the cited files. It is at backend-doctor/SKILL.md:120, deprecated in favour of `safety scan` and paired there with pip-audit. Severity: these are concrete example pins the agent will probably copy, so the risk of shipping an EOL runtime is real but not immediately breaking. Medium.

confirmed.title: docker-compose and .env.example produce a stack that won't start or connect
confirmed.evidence: postgres has no POSTGRES_PASSWORD. DATABASE_URL uses localhost inside the app container. A shared env_file gives JWT_SECRET to the db. `pg_isready -U postgres` hard-codes the user, and `version: "3.8"` is obsolete.
confirmed.impact: `docker compose up` fails, and the db container receives app secrets.
confirmed.recommendation: Use per-service env, POSTGRES_* in .env.example, service DNS names, a healthcheck with $${POSTGRES_USER}, and drop version:.

confirmed.title: GitHub Actions template lacks permissions (GHCR push fails) and uses static credentials
confirmed.evidence: No `permissions:` block while pushing to ghcr with GITHUB_TOKEN (read-only by default since 2023). Uppercase repo names are not lowercased. 'keep deployment credentials in CI secrets'.
confirmed.impact: The push fails with 403, or the job gets write-all tokens and long-lived cloud keys.
confirmed.recommendation: Use least-privilege permissions (packages: write only on push), lowercase image names, and OIDC federation.

confirmed.title: SLOs, alerting, incident response and runbooks are triggers but have no content
confirmed.evidence: :15 activates on SLIs/SLOs and runbooks, and the only content is the leaf ':404 ... + alerting rules'. Grep postmortem|on-call|error budget: 0.

confirmed.title: No scheduled jobs, job lifecycle, outbox relay or saga guidance
confirmed.evidence: Cron appears only in a table cell. Saga appears once. Grep temporal|advisory lock|leader|inbox: 0.
confirmed.impact: Jobs double-run across replicas, drop work on deploy, and multi-step flows have no compensation.
confirmed.recommendation: Add a jobs/workflows section: overlap locks, DST, worker drain, outbox relay with SKIP LOCKED/CDC plus inbox, sagas, and a durable-engine decision tree.
confirmed.verifierCorrection: Saying there is no outbox guidance is inaccurate. ops:182-187 defines the outbox pattern (same-transaction write, a relay process that polls and publishes, mark as processed), ops:392 routes to it, and implement:325 references it. ops:166-180 also covers job queues, idempotent consumers, ack-after-success, bounded retries, DLQ and visibility timeout. 'Saga appears once' is also wrong: it appears zero times. The real gap is scheduled jobs, worker lifecycle and sagas, plus a shallow outbox relay. That is medium, not high.

confirmed.title: Stacks beyond Node/Python/Go/Java are unsupported, and deploy hard-stops on them
confirmed.evidence: deploy :30 says 'stop' without package.json/pyproject/go.mod/pom/gradle. Grep php|laravel|dotnet|csproj|elixir|kotlin|deno: 0.

confirmed.recommendation: Add _shared/stacks/<lang>.md (manifests, test/lint/audit/migrate commands, Docker/CI) and replace the stop with ask.
confirmed.verifierCorrection: Rust and Ruby are recognised: context-loading.md:18 and :48 glob Cargo.toml and Gemfile, and scan:65-66 list both. The real defect is that deploy's manifest list is narrower than the shared one, so deploy stops on Rust and Ruby projects too. deploy stops and asks the user rather than refusing outright. doctor:70 says to 'fall back to the standard commands for the detected language', so it is not left with no commands at all. PHP, .NET, Kotlin DSL and Elixir are not covered at all. Medium rather than high, because the agent's own knowledge covers these stacks and the design skills are mostly language-agnostic.

confirmed.title: No guidance for LLM/AI feature backends (RAG, vector stores, LLM gateway)
confirmed.evidence: Grep LLM|RAG|vector|embedding|pgvector: 0. DB selection covers only PG/MySQL/Mongo/Redis.
confirmed.impact: LLM integrations ship with no timeouts, cost limits or prompt-injection defense.

A broader, cheaper fix is also missing: general resilience guidance for external dependencies (timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, budgets) in principles.md or backend-ops.

confirmed.title: No framework or dependency major-upgrade workflow (e.g. Spring Boot 2.7→3)
confirmed.evidence: Grep jakarta|openrewrite|upgrade|EOL: 0. refactor's HARD RULE forbids behavior change and doctor says only 'Check for breaking changes'.
confirmed.impact: Upgrades have no home skill, and the closest skill tells the agent to stop.

What is missing is a dependency or framework major-upgrade workflow: migration guides, stepwise version bumps, codemods, and an approved list of intended behaviour changes. That is an important enhancement, but medium rather than high.

confirmed.evidence: Loops back with no maximum. 'STOP. Fix issues, re-run' contradicts itself. The pause list omits push/CI/shared DB.
confirmed.impact: Implement↔test loops can run indefinitely, and Critical fixes happen without review.

confirmed.title: Scan detects Rust/Ruby with no decision tree and misses PHP, .NET, Kotlin, Elixir, Deno and Bun
confirmed.evidence: Trees cover only package.json, requirements/pyproject, go.mod and pom/gradle. No composer.json, csproj, mix.exs or deno.json.

confirmed.title: Staleness check misses code that reaches the branch through a merge commit
confirmed.evidence: The staleness rule runs `git log -1 --format=%ct -- src/` and treats memory as stale only if that committer time is newer than `## Last Updated`. Reproduced in a scratch repo: feature commit touching src/ at 2026-01-05, unrelated main commit on 01-06, `git merge --no-ff feat` at 01-10. `git log -1 --format=%ct -- src/` then returns 1767571200 (2026-01-05), not the merge time. History simplification drops the merge commit because it is TREESAME to its second parent, so the command reports the feature commit's older date.
confirmed.impact: Teams that use merge commits (GitHub's default merge button) get memory marked 'fresh' even after merged branches changed routes, schema or dependencies. Any refresh between a feature's last commit and its merge hides those changes, so every downstream skill works from stale memory it believes is current. F013's src/-only and timezone problems are separate.
confirmed.recommendation: Compare against what is actually on the branch, not commit dates. Store the HEAD SHA (or a hash of each manifest and source tree) when memory is written, then run `git diff --quiet <stored-sha> HEAD -- <paths>`, or `git log --first-parent -1 --format=%ct`. Record the SHA in each memory file's header.

confirmed.title: Memory files are merge-conflict-prone and have no locking or merge procedure for teams or parallel sessions
confirmed.location: memory-schema.md:14,57,102,143,187,227 (single `## Last Updated`), 234/260-270 (append at end), 305-311 (compaction rewrites); tool-rules.md:57-60; backend-scan/SKILL.md:127,147
confirmed.evidence: Every memory file has a single required `## Last Updated` line, and every skill run is told to 'refresh "Last Updated" timestamps' (scan:127, 147). New entries are appended as timestamped blocks at the end of the file. Compaction rewrites the head of the file and prunes entries. tool-rules.md:60 isolates concurrent features only for checkpoints ('Two concurrent features must not share a checkpoint'), while all features share the same memory files. Checkpoints (tool-rules.md:57) record no user or host, and tool-rules.md:58 tells any later run to 'offer to resume' an open checkpoint for the same skill. A search for 'merge conflict', 'lock' or 'concurrent' in memory-schema.md finds nothing.
confirmed.impact: If memory is committed, two developers (or two agent sessions on different branches) who both run any skill edit the same `Last Updated` line and append at the same end-of-file spot, which guarantees git conflicts. Conflict markers left in memory are then read as facts by the next skill. A teammate's committed checkpoint makes other people's runs offer to resume work they never started. Parallel sessions in one checkout can interleave appends and compaction. This is separate from F015, which only notes that VCS guidance is missing.
confirmed.recommendation: Pick and document a team model: either per-developer memory that is gitignored, or committed memory split into per-entry files (for example `decisions/<date>-<slug>.md`) with no shared `Last Updated` line, which merges cleanly. Add a lock file or atomic write-then-rename for memory updates. Add owner/host to checkpoints and gitignore `.checkpoints/`. Tell scan to detect conflict markers and stop instead of ingesting them.

confirmed.title: 200 KB memory size guard is far beyond what an agent can load, and scan's compaction never checks size

At roughly 4 bytes per token, 200 KB is about 50k tokens per file, so 150-200k tokens before any work starts. scan:151 compacts only by entry count ('If more than 5 exist'), never by size, and the guard is only checked 'before appending', never when reading.
confirmed.impact: A file can grow to many times what fits in a working context (for example a large endpoint inventory appended on each sync) and still pass the guard. Every skill then either truncates memory silently or burns its context window before doing anything. Because the guard never drops below 5 entries, five large entries can never be compacted under the limit.
confirmed.recommendation: Set a token-based budget per file (for example 8-16 KB) and check it on read as well as on write. Have compaction summarise older entries into a single 'current state' section instead of just moving them to archive. Note the per-invocation total context budget in context-loading.md.

confirmed.title: Implement's post-generation checklist is POSIX-only, despite the suite's cross-platform promise

confirmed.title: FastAPI and Gin handler snippets block the event loop or fall through after a bind error

Gin pattern (lines 295-299): `if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&dto); err != nil { /* 400 */ }` with no `return`, after which `h.svc.CreateUser(...)` is called anyway. F159 covers the Express snippets and F048 the TypeScript service snippet; these two are separate.
confirmed.impact: If the service is async (the norm with async SQLAlchemy), FastAPI gets an un-awaited coroutine and fails or returns garbage. If it is sync and does DB I/O, it blocks the event loop for every request because it runs inside `async def`. The Gin shape leads agents to write `c.JSON(400, ...)` without `return`, so invalid payloads still reach the service and the handler writes two responses. These are labelled the canonical 'Minimal' patterns the agent copies.

Gin: `if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&dto); err != nil { c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, ...); return }`, and show the error-mapping branch with `return` as well.

confirmed.title: Archive filenames can collide, so a later compaction can overwrite earlier archived history

confirmed.title: Memory files have no schema version, so memory written by earlier releases has no migration path
confirmed.evidence: Searching for 'version' in memory-schema.md finds only content fields ('primary languages and versions', 'database type and version'), with no schema or format version marker. The format has already changed. The initial commit's template (git show bbcc153:.opencode/everything-backend-memory/project-overview.md) used `## Purpose` and `## Tech Stack` sections written by the since-deleted `backend-discovery` and `backend-refresh-memory` skills (removed in b51c750). The current schema requires `## Type`, `## Structure` and `## Last Updated` (memory-schema.md:10-14). The staleness check (context-loading.md:128) depends on `## Last Updated`, which the old files lack.
confirmed.impact: Projects initialised with an earlier release keep memory that does not match the current schema. Scan sync appends to it in the new format, mixing both. The staleness check has no timestamp to read, so it behaves unpredictably, and nothing detects or upgrades the old format. This will recur with every schema change.
confirmed.recommendation: Add a front-matter header to each memory file (for example `schema: everything-backend-memory/2`, `written_by: <skill>@<version>`, `source_sha`). Have context-loading check it and send old or unversioned files to a scan `mode=migrate` that rewrites them into the current schema.

confirmed.title: Query-plan verification uses EXPLAIN ANALYZE with no warning that it executes the statement
confirmed.evidence: migrate:244-249 gives `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT ...` and says 'Compare plans before and after the migration'. Workflow step 7 (line 279) is 'Verify constraints, indexes, and query plans'. implement:268 says 'Check query plans or execution if the database supports it'. Neither skill says which database to run against or that ANALYZE actually runs the statement. In PostgreSQL, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on UPDATE, DELETE or INSERT, including the backfill statements in migrate:136-158, changes data unless wrapped in `BEGIN; ... ROLLBACK;`, and on large tables it does the full work.
confirmed.impact: An agent checking whether a backfill or repository UPDATE uses the new index can apply that write for real, possibly against whatever database `DATABASE_URL` points to, or run a full-cost query on a production-sized table. F025 covers DDL gates, not this verification step.
confirmed.recommendation: Use plain `EXPLAIN` by default. Allow `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` only on a disposable or staging database and, for DML, only inside `BEGIN; ... ROLLBACK;`. State the target database explicitly and require confirmation before running against any non-local database.

confirmed.title: No internationalization guidance: character sets, collation, Unicode normalization or localized responses
confirmed.evidence: A case-insensitive search for `utf|collat|charset|unicode|locale|i18n|l10n|Accept-Language|translat|timezone|currency` across `.agents/` matches only `FixedClock` in backend-test:110 and two 'concurrency' false positives. db-design recommends MySQL (70-73) with `VARCHAR(255)` columns but never says to use `utf8mb4` (MySQL's legacy `utf8` cannot store 4-byte characters such as emoji or some CJK). Uniqueness on emails and usernames has no Unicode normalization (NFC/NFKC) or IDN guidance. API error messages are fixed English strings with no `Accept-Language` or `Content-Language` handling, and `createdAt: string; // ISO timestamp` (api-design:157) sets no UTC or offset rule. F131 covers only case sensitivity and TIMESTAMP without time zone.
confirmed.impact: Generated schemas can silently truncate or reject multilingual data in MySQL. Visually identical Unicode identifiers can bypass uniqueness checks (homograph or duplicate accounts). APIs cannot serve localized errors. This matters for the suite's own audience: the README is translated into Indonesian, Spanish, Chinese and Japanese.
confirmed.recommendation: Add an i18n section to principles and db-design: utf8mb4 and an explicit collation for MySQL, a deliberate collation or ICU choice for PostgreSQL, NFKC plus case-fold normalization for identifiers, and UTC timestamps with explicit offsets in API payloads. In api-design, use machine-readable error codes with localized messages chosen via Accept-Language.

refuted.title: Gemini install target doesn't match Gemini CLI's documented layout
refuted.reason: The finding judges the target against Gemini CLI, but the README (line 62) and installer (94548bf:12-18) label it 'Gemini IDE', and the layout matches Google's Antigravity IDE plugin system. Antigravity's docs (antigravity.google/docs/plugins?tab=ide) say 'Save plugin folders to ~/.gemini/config/plugins/ to activate them across all IDE windows', and they describe a plugin as a directory defined by a plugin.json manifest, with skills as SKILL.md files. On this machine, Google's own plugins in ~/.gemini/config/plugins (android-cli-plugin, chrome-devtools-plugin, modern-web-guidance-plugin) use the same plugin.json (+ skills/) layout the installer writes. Gemini CLI users are also already covered by the 'Opencode / generic' ~/.agents/skills option, which Gemini CLI documents as an alias. At most there is a low-severity naming issue: the README says 'Gemini IDE' instead of Antigravity, and the generated plugin.json has only name and description, no version.

refuted.title: Questionable advice: WebSocket connections table, and an audit log that can capture secrets
refuted.reason: The audit-log secrets point is already handled. db-design L25 makes loading _shared/principles.md, including its security section, REQUIRED. principles.md L46 says 'Audit logging: ... exclude passwords, tokens, and secrets.' The recommendation to make the log append-only is already there: db-design L266 'Consider append-only storage'. Naming a column `timestamp` is valid in both PostgreSQL and MySQL, where it is a non-reserved keyword, so that is a style nitpick. 'WebSocket connections table' (L259) sits in a list of considerations. Persisting connection IDs is an established pattern, for example the canonical API Gateway WebSocket design that stores connectionIds in a table, and L258 already suggests Redis. None of this is materially wrong guidance.

refuted.title: backend-test duplicates text and generic advice
refuted.reason: The only real duplication is one 6-word bullet. backend-test/SKILL.md:65 ('Do not mock the unit under test', in the general Anti-patterns list) is repeated at :115 in the focused 'What NOT to mock' list, and a grep of .agents/skills finds that string only at those two lines. Repeating it in a mocking-specific checklist is defensible reinforcement and costs only a few tokens. The other cited range, :229-233, is not a duplicate. It is a two-line pointer: 'Use OpenCode tools during testing work. See `_shared/tool-rules.md`...'. The claim of 'generic advice' has no supporting evidence. The recommendation to 'move per-stack tables to references/' is also off target. backend-test has no tables, only a 14-line command block (:160-174) and a 4-line framework list (:210-213). No references/ directory exists anywhere in .agents/skills (find .agents -type d), so the repo has no such convention. At 260 lines, backend-test is already one of the shortest skills. This is a nitpick, not a real authoring-quality problem.

refuted.title: Inline templates inflate ops and deploy; there is no references/
refuted.reason: The evidence is inaccurate and the impact is minor. Counting code-block lines including fences gives 137 of 278 lines in deploy (about 49%, not 'about 70%') and 129 of 418 in ops. Both files are under the commonly recommended 500-line SKILL.md budget. Deploy's templates are Node-only (node:20-alpine, npm), so 'all stacks are loaded on every activation' does not apply to it. Ops:39 is a one-line pointer to `_shared/principles.md`, not a restatement. The only multi-stack inline block is ops:263-340, about 78 lines, so the token saving from a references/ split is small. No skill in the suite uses references/ (verified with find), so this is a suite-wide authoring choice rather than a defect in these two skills.
